Our correspondent has seen some impressive performances on this severe 7 Mile course which is generally reckoned to be at least one minute long. 1970's race, the 51st in the history, was to provde a brilliant win for the young Metropolitan Walking Club Phil Embleton.

On January 16th in Battersea Park Wilf Wesch completed 10 Miles in 70:55 2 minutes ahead of Phil Embleton. In the same race Barry Ingarfield recorded a personal best 78:16 with Dave McMullen finishing 6th in 82:58.
From the start it was Nihill and Embleton with the young Essex boy really pulling out all the stops to bring the European Champion to his first defeat in an incredible run of nearly four years.

Phil Embleton won his own promotion in a new record and another world class time. Wilf Wesch thrashed his german team mates for an impressive third place while Ray Middleton, Barry Ingarfield and John Moullin made up for the absence of some of our other stars to ensure that Belgrave won the team event.
Phil Embleton has broken 70 for 10 miles, 88 for 20 Kilometres and best of all the Track 10,000 Metres UK Record with a staggering sub 42 clocking.

In the AAA 10,000 metres Walk Championship on the Leicester Track Carl Lawton sped to a 46.31 second place behind Phil Embleton 45.26. Ray Middleton finished second in the Civil Service 3,000 metres in 14.02, Eric Hall was fifth in 14.50.

In the 20 Kilos, won by Phil Embleton Wilf Wesch finished 8th in 97.10. The other side of town saw Alan Callow and Barry Ingarfield covering 12,323 Metres and 12,276 metres to finish 13th and 15th respectively in the Highgate 1 Hour Track Walks.

Without Callow, Lawton, Middleton and Coates it was left to Ingarfield to lead the team home backed up by Len Duquemin, John Dunsford and sprightly Dave McMullen. Winner in a fast time was Phil Embleton.

Phil Embleton won this years race although he had a battle with Bill Sutherland for much of the distance. Carl Lawton started well down the field but gradually moved through to almost 2nd place but Sutherland's sprint finish was more than he could manage.
Once again it was Phil Embleton who led home. Carl Lawton was never in contention and in fact dropped back through the field as the race progressed and was caught by Ray Middleton with a lap to go.

JEAN MIDDLETON took part in a sponsored walk at Peckham Rye Park to raise funds for Leukemia Research, in memory of Phil Embleton. She raised over £60, a mighty effort, and sends thanks to all those who so generously sponsored her.
WC chalked up yet another win in his club's Phil Embleton Memorial 15Km event in Battersea Park on December 4th.
